facts.claim: First officers across major 737 MAX operators in the US command between $105,000 and $300,000 annually, and captains see baseline earnings starting between $262,000 and $288,000, with top-tier line-holders scaling well past $450,000.
A first-year first officer at United Airlines starts at $116 per hour, and senior captains on the narrowbody fleet see base rates climb past $360 per hour.
Flying a 737 MAX 8 pays identically to flying an older 737-800 or an Airbus A319 at legacy carriers because airlines group these airframes into a unified narrowbody pay category.
The monthly block hour guarantee typically secures 75 to 85 hours of pay per month, and premium open-time trips are often paid at 1.5 times or double the standard hourly scale.
Delta Air Lines set the initial benchmark with its post-pandemic contract and later offered a 31% salary increase, with United and American implementing matching step-ups.
An American Airlines 737 captain publicly posted a full-year W-2 showing gross earnings of $457,894.51, based in Miami with an hourly rate exceeding $360.

Southwest Airlines uses a trip-for-pay system; using the 1.149 conversion factor, a senior captain earns an hourly equivalent of roughly $347, over $330,000 at the 900-hour annual guarantee, with a 20% employer retirement contribution.
A first-year Boeing 737 first officer at American Airlines commands $118.31 per hour, rising to $181.93 after one year.

zh.title: 美國波音737 MAX機師年薪上看45萬美元　窄體機薪資追平廣體機
zh.summary: 美國主要航空公司737 MAX機師的年薪已大幅攀升：副機師約10.5萬至30萬美元，正機師基本年薪26.2萬至28.8萬美元起，資深者更可突破45萬美元；窄體機與廣體機的薪資差距已大幅縮小。
body: 美國主要航空公司737 MAX機師的薪資水準已創下歷史新高。副機師年薪介於10.5萬至30萬美元之間，正機師基本年薪自26.2萬至28.8萬美元起跳，資深航線機師更可突破45萬美元。薪資以時薪而非固定年薪計算：聯合航空首年副機師時薪116美元，資深窄體機正機師時薪則超過360美元。過去十年間，窄體機機師若無超時工作幾乎不可能年薪突破25萬美元，如今集體談判協議已大幅拉近窄體機與廣體機的基本薪資差距。

年資是決定薪資最關鍵的因素，但機型本身未必帶來加薪：在傳統航空公司，駕駛737 MAX 8與駕駛舊型737-800或空中巴士A319的薪資相同，因為業者將這些機型歸入同一窄體機薪資級距。總薪資取決於每月保證飛行時數，通常每月保證給付75至85小時；機師也可透過承接加班航班提高收入，部分加班時薪為標準時薪的1.5倍或2倍。達美航空以疫情後合約率先拉高薪資上限，隨後提供31%的加薪，聯合航空與美國航空也跟進調升窄體機隊薪資，以留住機師。

實際案例顯示天花板有多高：一名駐邁阿密的美國航空737正機師曾公開全年W-2稅單，總收入達457,894.51美元，其時薪超過360美元，並搭配加班獎勵與優質航班承接。西南航空採計程酬金（TFP）制而非傳統飛行時數制，依1.149換算係數折算，資深正機師時薪約347美元，以每年900小時保證時數計算，基本年薪超過33萬美元，另有高達20%的雇主退休提撥。不過高薪伴隨波動：機師須維持一級體檢合格，健康出狀況即可能立即停飛；資淺機師多在備勤多年，只能領取每月最低保證薪資，難以承接高薪加班航班。

en.title: How much do Boeing 737 MAX pilots earn at US carriers in 2026?
en.summary: Pay for Boeing 737 MAX pilots at major US carriers has climbed sharply: first officers earn roughly $105,000 to $300,000 a year, captains start at $262,000 to $288,000, and senior line-holders can pass $450,000, closing the historic gap with widebody pay.
body: Pay for Boeing 737 MAX pilots at major US carriers has reached historic highs. First officers command between $105,000 and $300,000 a year, while captains see baseline earnings starting between $262,000 and $288,000, with top-tier line-holders scaling well past $450,000. Compensation is driven by hourly rates rather than fixed salaries: a first-year first officer at United Airlines starts at $116 per hour, and senior captains on the narrowbody fleet see base rates climb past $360 per hour. Ten years ago, narrowbody pilots rarely crossed the $250,000 threshold without exhaustive schedules; modern collective bargaining agreements have compressed the historical gap between narrowbody and widebody base pay.

Seniority is the single most critical factor governing pay, but aircraft type does not automatically dictate premium pay: flying a 737 MAX 8 pays identically to flying an older 737-800 or an Airbus A319 at legacy carriers, because airlines group these airframes into a unified narrowbody pay category. Total compensation hinges on the monthly block hour guarantee, which typically secures 75 to 85 hours of pay per month; pilots who bid premium open-time trips can earn 1.5 times or double the standard hourly scale. Delta Air Lines set the initial benchmark with its post-pandemic contract and later offered a 31% salary increase, pushing United Airlines and American Airlines to implement matching step-ups across their narrowbody fleets.

The ceiling became concrete when an American Airlines 737 captain publicly posted a full-year W-2 document showing gross earnings of $457,894.51. The Miami-based pilot capitalized on an hourly rate exceeding $360 combined with premium flight incentives and premium open-time pick-ups. Southwest Airlines, which uses a trip-for-pay system rather than traditional block hours, offers the highest narrowbody-only pay ceiling in US aviation: using the 1.149 conversion factor, a senior Southwest captain earns an hourly equivalent of roughly $347, translating to a baseline salary of over $330,000 at the standard 900-hour annual guarantee, backed by a 20% total employer retirement contribution. The high pay carries caveats: compensation depends on maintaining an unblemished first-class medical certificate, and junior pilots often spend years on reserve, restricted to the baseline minimum monthly guarantee.
